tools.name: list_tools
tools.title: List the dashboard's tools
tools.description:
List every dashboard tool by name, with a one-line summary, grouped by area (messages,
updates, work, requests, docs, channels, sessions, secrets, media, apps, feedback).

This server shows only three tools so your context stays small: list_tools to find a tool,
describe_tools to read its arguments, and call_tool to run it.

Argument: query (optional), words to filter by. A tool is listed when every word appears in
its name, its area, its summary or its description, in any case: "secret", "doc", "upload".

query.description: Words to filter by, e.g. "secret" or "edit doc". Omit to list every tool.

tools.name: describe_tools
tools.title: Read tools' arguments
tools.description:
Get the full description and JSON input schema of up to 20 dashboard tools, exactly as a
client that lists every tool would see them. Call it before you use a tool for the first
time, then run the tool with call_tool.

Argument: names, the tool names from list_tools, e.g. ["post_update", "set_status"].
A name that matches no tool comes back under unknown.

names.description: Tool names, from list_tools. At most 20.

tools.name: call_tool
tools.title: Run a dashboard tool
tools.description:
Run one dashboard tool by name. It behaves exactly as calling that tool directly: the same
permissions, the same checks on its arguments, the same errors and the same answer.

Arguments:
- name: the tool, from list_tools, e.g. "post_message".
- arguments: that tool's own arguments, as describe_tools shows them, e.g.
  { "update_id": "…", "body": "Done: the build is green." }. Omit for a tool that takes none.

Example: call_tool({ name: "acknowledge", arguments: { message_id: "…", state: "thinking" } }).

An unknown name says so: call list_tools to find the right one. Wrong arguments come back
with the tool's own validation error: call describe_tools for its schema and try again.

name.description: The tool to run, from list_tools.

arguments.description: The tool's own arguments, as describe_tools shows them. Omit for none.
